skill.name: agy-worker
skill.description: Use when Codex should delegate repository exploration or implementation to Google Antigravity CLI (agy), then review, verify, repair, and deliver the result.
skill.summary: Delegate bounded repository work to Google Antigravity, then review and verify the resulting changes.
skill.author: cagdasyurekli

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are parser noise, documentation, validation guards, or bounded local orchestration. Confirmed risks include the approved external provider launch, arbitrary approved verifier execution, third-party repository transmission, and default session mode with normal user authority. The static review covers only 400 representative findings, so the remaining analyzer matches still require manual review before publication. Static review was capped at 400/993 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 593 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Session isolation is the default even though it grants normal user filesystem and network authority.
remediation.suggestion: Default to native containment where supported, and require a prominent per-launch warning when session mode is selected.

remediation.issue: Approved repository content can be transmitted to Google or Gemini.
remediation.suggestion: Require selected-content staging by default, block known secret paths, and display the exact transmitted file list before approval.

remediation.issue: Legacy verifier mode executes caller-supplied text through bash -c.
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell verification from normal workflows and require canonical argv verification under native containment.

remediation.issue: The analyzer presented only 400 of 993 static matches for adjudication.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the 593 unpresented matches before enabling automatic marketplace publication.

content.value_statement: Complex repository tasks require controlled delegation and independent verification. This skill stages approved content, runs Antigravity, and binds review evidence to each candidate.
actual_capabilities: Previews provider-readable repository content before dispatch.
Stages approved files in a private Gitless workspace for scoped jobs.
Delegates exploration, implementation, and project work to the agy CLI.
Tracks job state, time limits, continuation, cancellation, and preserved results.
Creates isolated verification copies and runs driver-selected checks.
Binds approvals, candidate bytes, verification evidence, and final disposition with digests.
limitations: The host integration supports Codex only, not Claude or Claude Code.
Live delegation requires Bash, Python, Git, agy, provider authentication, and network access.
The default session mode does not provide host containment for the provider.
Worker output remains untrusted until Codex reviews the diff and runs relevant checks.

use_cases.title: Delegate a bounded feature
use_cases.description: Stage selected files, request a focused implementation, inspect the diff, and verify the candidate before acceptance.

use_cases.title: Expand test coverage
use_cases.description: Delegate test creation within an approved scope, then run project tests against an isolated candidate copy.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a broad project change
use_cases.description: Use several controlled cycles for a larger change while retaining explicit approval and final review authority.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a repository area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agy-worker to explore [area]. Read only [paths]. Report findings and uncertainties without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a focused change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agy-worker to implement [change]. Allow edits only under [paths]. Verify with [test command] and review the final diff.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a verified failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the approved agy-worker job. Provide the sanitized failure from [check]. Keep the existing scope, model, and budget.

prompt_templates.title: Run a governed project workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project workflow for [goal]. Approve only [content scope], use [isolation mode], and cap work at [cycles]. Run [checks] before finalization.

output_examples.input: Explore the parser and identify missing error-path tests.

best_practices: Prefer selected-content staging and review every provider-readable path before approval.
Use exact argv verification and provide only the environment variables required by each check.
Inspect candidate bytes and rerun affected checks before assigning a final disposition.
anti_patterns: Do not approve a whole worktree that contains secrets or unrelated private files.
Do not treat provider output or worker-reported tests as independent verification.
Do not use session isolation when the provider must lack normal user filesystem authority.

faq.question: Which host tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Codex. Claude and Claude Code are included as search terms but are not supported hosts.

faq.question: Does installation authorize repository transmission?
faq.answer: No. Each launch requires an explicit approval that binds the readable content, isolation mode, task, model, and budget.

faq.question: Can the provider read the entire worktree?
faq.answer: Yes, when whole-worktree mode is approved. Selected-content mode limits the staged repository content but does not contain the host in session mode.

faq.question: Does the skill verify worker claims automatically?
faq.answer: No. Codex must review the actual candidate and run suitable driver-owned checks before acceptance.

faq.question: Can verification commands access credentials?
faq.answer: Only explicitly selected variables are passed. Credential-like variables and shell verification require separate acknowledgments.

faq.question: What happens when a check fails?
faq.answer: The candidate is preserved. An approved same-scope repair can receive sanitized failure details, or the job can finish with a limited disposition.
